findings.F1: The size of the breakout day barely changes what follows. On the 381 independent breakouts (the first bar of each cluster), the excess 10-day return was +1.34 pp in the bottom half of the forecast (n=151, t=1.15) and +1.94 pp in the top half (n=230, t=1.65), a gap of about 0.6 pp. By forecast quintile the means were 3.42 / −0.46 / 2.44 / 1.82 / 1.28 pp, with no ordering.
findings.F2: The result is unclear because the effect is tiny next to the noise. The per-breakout standard deviation is 14–18 pp against a difference of about 1–2 pp. With roughly 380 clusters, the standard error of the gap is near 1.5 pp, so neither the reject rule (|t| ≥ 2) nor the ±1 pp equivalence test can be reached.
findings.F3: The calendar year drowns the breakout effect, and both halves move together. Excess 10-day returns after breakouts were negative in both halves in 2018 (−4.8 / −4.2 pp, n=17/24, hit 24%/25%) and in 2022 (−2.5 / −3.9 pp, n=19/27). They were positive in both halves in 2020 (+7.0 / +5.5 pp, n=22/33, t=2.56/1.94).
findings.F4: Breakouts in coins with a mildly positive 60-day return had the strongest follow-through. Where the 60-day return was 0–30%, excess returns were +3.8 pp (bottom half, n=24) and +6.6 pp (top half, n=31, t=1.79, hit 61%). Where the 60-day return was negative or not yet available, they were about +1.0 pp in both halves (n=114/172, t≈0.75). Where it was above 30%, the top half gave +2.9 pp (n=27) and the bottom half −0.4 pp (n=13).
findings.F5: The positive mean after outsized breakout days comes from a few large winners. The top half's mean was +1.94 pp but its median was −1.39 pp, with a hit rate of 49.6% (n=230). The smallest-quintile breakouts had a mean of +3.42 pp, a median of +1.50 pp and a hit rate of 59.7% (n=77, t=2.11).
findings.F6: Holding on to breakout runs after their first day showed a mild edge on non-overlapping samples, with large outsized days doing somewhat better. On every 10th positive-forecast bar, the top half gave +3.99 pp (n=98, t=1.75) and the bottom half +1.70 pp (n=97, t=0.89).

ideas.idea: A coin's new 20-day closing high, made while its close is above the close of 60 days earlier but by less than about 30%, is followed by a 10-day rise larger than the coin's average 10-day rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would take breakouts that come after a moderate prior advance and skip those that come out of a falling or flat 60-day stretch.
ideas.name: breakout after moderate prior advance

ideas.idea: A coin's new 20-day closing high made on a small up day is followed by a rise over the next 10 days more often than after an average day of that coin.
ideas.consequence: A trader would not require an outsized breakout day before going long; quiet new highs are at least as reliable in how often they work.
ideas.name: quiet new highs persist

ideas.idea: When a coin keeps printing new 20-day closing highs within ten days of earlier ones, its 10-day forward rise is larger than its average 10-day rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would add to or keep longs in coins already in an established run of new highs, rather than only buying the first break.
ideas.name: repeated highs extend trend
